responsibility.value: Serves as the application's single EF Core DbContext — owns all DbSet definitions, applies multi-tenant global query filters on ITenantScoped entities via OnModelCreating reflection, auto-stamps AuditableEntity timestamps on SaveChangesAsync, and seeds reference data on first migration.

Owns: Applying tenant-scoped HasQueryFilter to every ITenantScoped entity type via OnModelCreating reflection over model entity types
Applying additional multi-store query filters on InstrumentRental (only active instruments) and Announcement (active + store-gated)
Auto-stamping CreatedAt / UpdatedAt on AuditableEntity entries before each SaveChangesAsync
Exposing BeginTransactionAsync for callers that need multi-step atomic operations
Delegating seed data to ModelBuilderSeed.Seed during model creation
Lazy-resolving the current store ID via ICurrentActor.GetCurrentStoreId() with graceful StoreNotResolvedException fallback for non-store roles
doesNotOwn: Identity user/role management — delegated to the IdentityDbContext<AppUser, AppRole, int> base class and ASP.NET Core Identity's own store
Tenant identity resolution — that lives in ICurrentActor (CurrentActor), which this context calls synchronously via GetStoreId() during query filter evaluation
Migration execution — the MigrationRunner service handles applying pending migrations at startup

collaborators.detail: Implements the application-level DbContext abstraction so services depend on the interface, not the concrete EF Core type
Injected via primary constructor; GetCurrentStoreId() is called inside the tenant-query-filter reflection loop and the lazy GetStoreId() helper
Injected via primary constructor; clock.UtcNow is used in the SaveChangesAsync override to stamp AuditableEntity timestamps
OnModelCreating iterates all entity types and applies HasQueryFilter to those implementing ITenantScoped
SaveChangesAsync checks ChangeTracker.Entries<AuditableEntity>() for entities that need CreatedAt/UpdatedAt stamping
ModelBuilderSeed.Seed(modelBuilder) is called at the end of OnModelCreating to populate seed data

contracts: All ITenantScoped entities have a global query filter that restricts rows to the current store ID (or returns all rows if the current actor is not a store employee)
Every AuditableEntity has its CreatedAt set to IClock.UtcNow on insert and UpdatedAt on modification
StoreNotResolvedException during tenant filter resolution is silently caught — queries return empty results for non-store roles rather than throwing
InstrumentRental and Announcement have additional active-status filters beyond the ITenantScoped tenant filter
assumptions: ICurrentActor.GetCurrentStoreId() returns a cached/intra-request value — this method is called during LINQ query filter evaluation (synchronous), so any database call inside it would cause an N+1 disaster inside every EF query. The pre-warming in TenantInitializationMiddleware ensures the value is already cached before any query runs.
The single-StoreId model is a business constraint — a user belongs to at most one active MusicStore; employees with multiple active store affiliations are not supported by this schema design.
ModelBuilderSeed.Seed is safe to run on every model creation (migrations) — it uses HasData which is idempotent under migration application.
invariants: Every SaveChangesAsync call stamps AuditableEntity timestamps before persisting — no entity slips through without audit timestamps when going through this context
Query filters are applied once at model build time — they cannot be disabled per-query without injecting a separate DbContext instance or raw SQL
failureModes: A StoreNotResolvedException rising out of GetStoreId() during query filter evaluation would cause an HTTP 500 on every DB-touching endpoint for non-store roles — the try/catch in GetStoreId() prevents this
If ICurrentActor.GetCurrentStoreId() is not pre-warmed and performs a DB lookup synchronously inside a LINQ query filter, it causes a catastrophic N+1 locking scenario and potential deadlock

Migrations that add new ITenantScoped entity types automatically get the tenant filter without any additional per-entity wiring — this is correct by design but makes it easy to forget the security implications
architecturalNotes: HIGH BLAST RADIUS — every application-layer service depends on IAppDbContext, which resolves to this class. A behavioral change, performance regression, or connection-string issue here affects the entire API surface.

The GetStoreId() / SetTenantFilter reflection pattern is fragile under assembly trimming or NativeAOT — it relies on MakeGenericMethod with runtime-discovered types, which trim analysis cannot see statically.

The dual-filter model (ITenantScoped.HasQueryFilter + entity-specific filters on InstrumentRental/Announcement) creates a subtle ordering constraint: the tenant filter must not conflict with the active-status filter on InstrumentRental.
IClock is used instead of DateTime.UtcNow directly, enabling deterministic time in tests.
